p: Next, a contact sheet: ONE square image divided into a 2 x 2 grid of four equal square panels with thin plain gaps between them. Each panel is a separate studio product photo in exactly the master style (same warm grey backdrop, same lighting, same three-quarter front-left angle, object filling about 80% of its panel, matte black finish unless stated, unbranded, no text, no people). Top left: A set of landmine handles, a steel sleeve that slides onto the end of a barbell, fitted with a choice of grips: a pair of neutral handles in a V shape, a wide T handle or two parallel overhead press handles. Top right: A set of chains, a pair of heavy steel link chains, each draped over a thinner loading chain, hanging from both sleeves of a barbell so the links pile on the floor. Bottom left: A set of thick grips, a pair of thick rubber tubular sleeves with a slit along their length, made to clip around a bar or dumbbell handle to widen it. Bottom right: A power rack / squat rack, a tall four-post steel cage with holes punched up each upright, J-hooks holding a barbell at shoulder height, horizontal safety bars running front to back at waist height inside the cage and a pull-up bar across the top.

Top left: A bench press station, a flat padded bench joined to a pair of steel uprights at the head end with bar catches at two heights, a barbell resting in the catches and plate storage horns on the uprights. Top right: An incline bench station, a fixed incline back pad at about 30 to 45 degrees with a small seat, tall steel uprights behind the head holding a barbell, and a raised spotter platform at the rear. Bottom left: A shoulder press bench, a near-upright padded backrest with a small seat, tall steel uprights behind the head holding a barbell overhead and a footrest platform for a spotter at the back. Bottom right: A preacher bench, a seat in front of an angled padded arm rest sloping down and away from the user, with a pair of bar catches at the base of the pad to rest an EZ bar.

Top right: An adjustable kettlebell, a kettlebell made of a handle and core that accepts stacked weight plates locked into its base, with a selector dial or locking pin. Bottom left: A set of clubbells / Indian clubs, a pair of bowling-pin-shaped steel or wooden clubs, narrow at the knurled handle and widening to a heavy rounded end. Bottom right: A steel mace, a long steel bar about 1 m long with a heavy steel ball welded to one end and a knurled shaft, standing upright on the ball end.
